title: What is money? How money differs from an asset.
subtitle: Money is a medium of exchange, not the end goal itself.
openingQuestion: Why did gold become money throughout history, while a stone or a shirt never did?
openingOptions: Because ancient governments mandated that every transaction be settled in gold
Because gold's colour and shine are simply more attractive than stone or other natural materials
Because gold is divisible, durable, scarce, easily recognised, and widely accepted
Because gold is light in weight and much easier to carry long distances than stone
explanation: Money needs five properties: it must be divisible, durable, uniform, scarce, and widely accepted. Gold meets all five; stone is too bulky to divide and inconsistent in shape, while clothing is neither durable nor scarce - which is why neither ever became widely used currency.

diagram.label: Bartering goods for goods: hard to match needs
A go-between is needed: durable, divisible, scarce
Once widely accepted, it becomes money

realWorldExample.description: Today's VND is not backed by gold but by trust in the state and its monetary policy.

quiz.question: What is the single most important difference between money and an asset?
options: An asset is always worth more than cash at the same point in time
Money is created by banks, while assets are created by businesses
Money can be spent right away; an asset must be sold to become money
Money earns interest over time, while an asset never does
quiz.explanation: Cash is the most liquid asset there is: you can use it immediately. Stocks, real estate and gold are all assets, but each takes time and cost to convert into money.

quiz.question: What is your net worth?
options: The value of the house and car you currently own
The balance across all of your bank accounts
Your total income minus your total expenses for the year
Your total assets minus your total liabilities
quiz.explanation: Net worth = assets − liabilities. Someone earning 100 million a month but owing 5 billion can have a negative net worth. Someone earning 15 million who has saved steadily for 10 years can have a positive one.

quiz.question: How does inflation affect cash and real assets differently?
options: Real assets lose value faster than cash does under inflation
Both cash and real assets lose value in exactly the same way
Cash loses purchasing power; real assets tend to hold their value
Money in a bank savings account is untouched by inflation
quiz.explanation: Holding cash when inflation runs at 6% means losing 6% of purchasing power every year. This is exactly why investing matters: to earn a return that outruns inflation.

quiz.question: Scenario: You have 500 million VND. Option A: keep it as cash at home. Option B: buy gold (gold price rises 5% a year on average, inflation runs at 4% a year). After 3 years, which option preserves purchasing power better, and by roughly how much?
options: A is better, because cash carries no price-volatility risk
B is better, by roughly 15% (3% × 3 years)
The two are equivalent, because gold also loses value
B is better, but only by roughly 3% (1% × 3 years)
quiz.explanation: Cash loses about 4% a year to inflation, so after 3 years it has lost roughly 12% of its purchasing power. Gold gains about 5% a year, so after 3 years its nominal value is up roughly 15%. Gold's real return is about 1% a year (5% − 4%). Gold preserves purchasing power better than cash in an inflationary environment.

quiz.question: Scenario: You own 2 billion VND of real estate and 5 million in cash. Why might you still run into financial trouble?
options: Because your net worth turns negative once most of it sits in real estate
Because real estate is not counted toward net worth at all
Because the asset is large but illiquid, so it can't cover an immediate bill
Because a property's price always falls whenever you need to sell it fast
quiz.explanation: Being rich on the balance sheet and having money to spend are two different things. Selling a house takes months, so when a bill falls due, that 2 billion does nothing to help - which is exactly why cash is classed separately from every other asset.

keyTakeaways: Money is a medium of exchange with absolute liquidity
Net worth = total assets − total liabilities
Cash loses purchasing power to inflation; investing exists to preserve real value

practicePrompt.question: If inflation rises, what happens to the real value of 500 million VND you're holding in cash?
options: It stays the same, because money is still money
It rises, provided you don't spend it
It rises, because cash is easy to spend
It falls, because purchasing power erodes
practicePrompt.explanation: Cash keeps the same face amount but loses purchasing power as prices rise. This is why preserving real value is an important financial goal.

summary.keyIdea: Money is a tool for exchange, while an asset is something that can create or hold value.
summary.formula: Net worth = total assets − total liabilities.
summary.commonMistake: Confusing cash with an asset that holds real value.
summary.action: Calculate your own net worth by listing your current assets and liabilities.

application.title: Apply it now
application.message: Don't just look at the figure in your account; also look at its real value after inflation.

sections.text: Gold served as a global currency for thousands of years. Precious stones, shells, or clothing never became widely used money. The difference lies in five properties that anything aspiring to be 'money' has to have.
The five required properties of money

For something to become widely accepted money, it needs to be: divisible (splitting an amount of gold into smaller pieces preserves proportional value), durable (it doesn't degrade over time), uniform (one tael of gold is the same wherever it is), scarce (it cannot be produced without limit), and widely accepted (many people agree to use it in exchange).

items: Divisible: gold can be split into smaller units without losing proportional value
Durable: gold does not rust or decay across hundreds of years
Uniform: 1 tael of 24K gold in Vietnam is identical to one in the US
Scarce: the amount of gold that can be mined has a natural limit
Widely accepted: nearly every civilisation has recognised gold's value

sections.text: Why didn't stone or clothing become money?

Stone is too bulky to divide and transport, and inconsistent in shape and size. Clothing isn't durable (it tears and wears out over time) and isn't scarce (anyone can sew more). Missing even one of the five properties makes something a poor long-term medium of exchange.
How does money differ from an asset?

Money is a medium of exchange - a tool for measuring and transferring value. An asset is something that creates or stores value (stocks, real estate, gold when not used for a transaction). The problem with cash: it loses purchasing power to inflation every year, while an asset has the potential to gain real value over time.

sections.label: Net worth
sections.text: Net worth = total assets − total liabilities. This figure reflects a person's financial position far more accurately than simply looking at a bank account balance.

lines: Understanding what money truly is is the first step to not confusing 'holding money' with 'holding value' - two things that look alike but are entirely different over the long run.
